headline: High-risk write-capable pair: Plandex can modify local files and git while the other agent has allowlisted egress, creating dangerous interaction and leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented shared channel, but B reads and writes project files by default and can act on file content; if A's outputs are copied into B's workspace, prompt injection becomes plausible. A's docs-only profile does not show a parser, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A's output is pasted into B's project directory or stdin/stdout workflow
IF B treats file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Disable auto-apply in B
Require a human review step before B executes file-derived instructions
Prefix imported text as untrusted data
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read the filesystem and has broad egress, so any sensitive material in shared files could be transmitted outward. A is docs-only and shows allowlisted egress, but the pair still creates a leakage path if A's outputs or inputs contain secrets. The shared-workspace assumption is not proven, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF sensitive files are present in that directory
IF B forwards file contents to its model provider or Plandex Cloud
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace
Run B with a scrubbed project copy
Restrict B's network egress to approved endpoints
Rotate any secrets exposed in the workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while A's profile does not show any locking or coordination. If A also writes through its allowlisted workflow or emits changes consumed by B, concurrent edits can corrupt git state or overwrite work. Uncertainty about A's write surface escalates this to high because the pairwise conflict is plausible and B's defaults are mutable.
conditions: IF A produces artifacts that B applies into the same repository
IF two B instances or A+B touch the same git branch without locking
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other applies changes
Require git status checks before apply
Limit B to a throwaway clone
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or merge arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: B's review-then-apply flow can still treat upstream output as actionable, and A is a research agent whose outputs may be used as inputs for coding tasks. There is no direct evidence of verification between them, so the cascade is plausible but not proven. Because B has explicit apply authority, the blast radius can extend beyond a single document.
conditions: IF B consumes A's generated text, code, or recommendations as task input
IF B auto-applies changes without a separate verification step
mitigations: Require B to cite source files before applying changes
Turn off auto-apply
Add a second human review for A-derived outputs
Compare outputs against tests before execution
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and A touches no data classes while B touches source code only. The only concrete compliance concern is that B handles model-provider API keys, but the pair does not show a regulated-data pathway. One-agent-only citations are sufficient here because the issue is B's handling surface, not an interaction-specific breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B's project directory
IF the deployment environment requires a specific residency or retention policy not shown here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Review B's retention settings
Store API keys in a dedicated secret manager
Document the data handling policy before use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
